entities.summary:
Wei Yan, courtesy name Wenchang, was a Chinese military general and politician of the state of Shu Han during the Three Kingdoms period of China.

Originally a subordinate of the warlord Liu Bei during the late Eastern Han dynasty, Wei Yan rose through the ranks and became a general after Liu Bei seized control of Yi Province in 214.

His performance in battle helped him to become a prominent figure in the Shu military in a short period of time. He was later appointed as the Administrator of Hanzhong Province.

Wei Yan played a crucial role in several key battles, including the Battle of Red Cliffs, which showcased his strategic prowess and helped secure a significant victory for Shu Han.

He also oversaw the construction of several key infrastructure projects, including the construction of the Longmen Grottoes, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Wei Yan's legacy extends beyond his military accomplishments, as he also served as a model for future generations of Chinese leaders, emphasizing the importance of education, integrity, and public service.

As a testament to his enduring impact, Wei Yan's name has been invoked in popular culture, including in films, literature, and art, solidifying his place in the collective imagination of China.

Despite the passage of centuries, Wei Yan's contributions continue to inspire new generations of scholars, historians, and enthusiasts, cementing his status as one of China's most celebrated figures in the annals of history.
